source.title: Target alignment in truncated kernel ridge regression
source.authors: A. Amini; R. Baumgartner; Dai Feng

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes and simulates test-risk curves for truncated kernel ridge regression, a different model class and method from the original deep-network studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for TKRR risk as a function of truncation level and regularization, including effects of noise. Its polynomial-alignment rate results and comparisons of minimum risk versus sample size do not test the listed double-descent versions. Numerical curve values are presented only in figures.
record.test_reason: The study cites double descent as motivation but tests none of the listed versions. Its 'double descent' is an MSE curve over truncation level r for synthetic two-band targets. There r stays far below n (r≤50, n=200) with fixed λ>0, so no interpolation threshold is crossed. Per Proposition 2(a), the rise comes from the variance term between alignment bands, and the second descent comes from entering the second band. Its 'multiple descent' curves are over the ridge parameter λ, not model size, epochs or samples. These are related constructs: target-alignment-driven non-monotonicity in kernel methods. They are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. More precisely: target-alignment spectra predict KRR/TKRR generalization, and TKRR attains faster rates than full KRR in the over-aligned polynomial regime. For bandlimited alignment, λ-regularization curves show multiple descent and a noise-dependent phase transition, and r-truncation curves show double descent. Narrower, lower-index alignment spectra give lower error.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses theoretical analysis and simulations of fixed-design kernel ridge regression and truncated kernel ridge regression, rather than deep-network size, epoch, or sample-size sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported risk-curve behavior changes with noise level; the theoretical turning-point condition also depends on truncation level and regularization. Alignment-spectrum placement and concentration affect generalization error.

fits_no_version.finding: In fixed-design TKRR with bandlimited target alignment, MSE vs truncation level r rises between alignment bands and falls within them. With two bands this gives a 'double descent'-shaped r-curve whose rise depends on noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-monotone (multi-descent) risk in capacity-like parameters can arise from the target's alignment spectrum relative to the kernel eigenbasis, without an interpolation threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: The MSE vs −log(λ) regularization curve moves from monotone decreasing at σ=0, to non-monotone at moderate σ, to monotone increasing at large σ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The shape of the ridge-regularization risk curve, including multiple descent, depends on the noise level for bandlimited targets in KRR.

record.problems: The empirical demonstrations are simulations with bandlimited synthetic targets and fixed design. Curve values are figure-only, and the paper does not test neural networks, epoch-wise curves, an interpolation-threshold location, or the effect of optimally tuned regularization on the presence of multiple descent.
record.rows_left_out: The polynomial-alignment rate results and the comparison of minimum MSE versus sample size in Appendix C were not extracted as rows because they do not report the double-descent behaviors named by the tested versions. No relevant reported curve results were omitted.

untested.parts: All: no deep networks or model-size sweep.
All: sample-size results (Appendix C) report only minimum MSE rates, not non-monotonicity in n.
Descent past an interpolation point, and subsuming the U-curve; truncation never reaches interpolation.
A label-noise-driven interpolation peak, multiple peaks along a capacity axis, and removal under optimal regularization.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's labels were removed. The record's V4 'supports' rests on calling an r-curve with no interpolation point double descent. The V6 'supports' rests on λ-axis curves rather than a capacity-axis peak. All evidence is figure-only synthetic simulation (Gaussian kernel, d=4, n=200).

versions.untested_parts: Deep-network model-size sweeps and the peak near the size that just fits the training set.
Whether increasing sample size near an interpolation threshold raises test error.
The study tests TKRR truncation-risk curves, not a range of model classes; it does not locate an interpolation point or establish that the curve subsumes the classical U-shaped curve.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak location across size, epochs, and sample size.

The study varies additive noise and reports non-monotone curves, but does not establish that the peak is caused specifically by label noise or variance, test multiple peaks under optimally tuned regularization, or show that optimal tuning removes them.
Whether re-expressing complexity as an effective number of parameters turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: TKRR
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical expected MSE as a function of truncation level r for bandlimited target alignment.

conditions.value: σ²/n; monotonicity condition depends on (σ²/n)b and λ/μ_l+1

rows.measure: Expected empirical MSE versus truncation level r
rows.value: MSE increases on [1,l] and [l+b+1,n]; between these intervals it is nondecreasing up to j* and decreasing from j* to l+b. If (σ²/n)b < 1 + 2λ/μ_l+1, it decreases over the full interval [l+1,l+1+b].
rows.note: The paper gives a theoretical non-monotone risk pattern and states that the turning point depends on the noise level, truncation, and regularization parameters.
rows.check: Theoretical MSE vs truncation r is non-monotone because of where the alignment band sits, not because of an interpolation point. r<n, λ>0 and nothing interpolates, so it cannot show V4's post-interpolation descent. The noise condition governs the within-band decrease, not a label-noise-driven interpolation peak, so it does not bear on V6.

rows.subject: TKRR
rows.operation_detail: Simulated expected MSE versus −log(λ) at different noise levels.
rows.note: The text describes the curve as monotonically decreasing at zero noise.
rows.check: The curve is over the regularization parameter λ, not a capacity, epoch or sample axis named by any version. It is monotone decreasing at σ=0. 'Absent' presumes a version's effect is measurable here, which it is not.

rows.subject: TKRR
rows.operation_detail: Simulated expected MSE versus −log(λ) at different noise levels.

conditions.value: moderate σ; exact values not stated

rows.note: The text describes non-monotonic behavior at moderate noise levels.
rows.check: The non-monotone λ-curve at moderate noise is on the regularization axis, not size, epochs or samples. The figure gives no σ values beyond the panel labels (s=2.4–4), and the text only says 'moderate'.

rows.subject: TKRR
rows.operation_detail: Simulated expected MSE versus −log(λ) at different noise levels.

conditions.value: large σ; exact values not stated

rows.note: The text describes the curve as monotonically increasing at large noise; this is monotone rather than a non-monotone descent curve.
rows.check: A monotone increasing λ-curve at large σ is not the opposite of any version's effect, so 'reversed' is wrong. It is a regularization curve, not a capacity curve.

rows.subject: TKRR
rows.operation_detail: Simulated expected MSE versus truncation level r for a target with two non-overlapping alignment bands.

conditions.value: two non-overlapping bands; l1=0, l2=30, b=10
σ/√n varied; plotted values include 0, 0.06, 0.12, 0.18, 0.24, and 0.3

rows.measure: Expected MSE versus truncation level r
rows.note: The authors describe the curves as showing double descent and a phase transition. The result is reported for the plotted set of noise levels in aggregate; the text does not assign a separate curve shape to each level.
rows.check: The authors call the r-curve 'double-descent', but r≤50 with n=200 and fixed λ, so there is no interpolation threshold. The rise between bands is variance-only, and the second descent reflects target structure in the second band. This is a different mechanism from V4. Values are figure-only.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
